⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Mughirah, from Ibn Umar, who said: It is the zakah.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ali, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Zayd ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from Hassan ibn Mukhariq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: the zakah.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah and al-Hasan: al-Ma'un: the obligatory zakah.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Umar, from Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: It is the zakah.

⁕ I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾: He said: The zakah.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾: They are the hypocrites who withhold the zakah of their wealth.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: the obligatory zakah.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Uqbah narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾: They withheld the charities of their wealth, so Allah reproached them for it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan: ﴿Those who make show [of their deeds] and withhold al-Ma'un﴾. He said: It is the hypocrite who withholds the zakah of his wealth. If he prays, he makes a show, and if he misses it, he does not regret it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Salamah, from al-Dahhak, who said: It is the zakah.

Others said: It is what people lend to one another among themselves, such as the bucket, the cooking pot and the like.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Hakam ibn Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from Abu al-Abidin, that he said to Abdullah: Inform me about al-Ma'un. He said: It is what people lend to one another among themselves.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Yahya ibn al-Jazzar narrate from Abu al-Abidin, a man from Banu Tamim who was blind, and who used to ask Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and Ibn Mas'ud would recognise that about him. He asked Abdullah about al-Ma'un, and Abdullah said: Among al-Ma'un is withholding the axe, the cooking pot and the bucket: two qualities out of these three. Shu'bah said: As for the axe, there is no doubt about it.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from Abu al-Abidin, from Abdullah, the like of it.

⁕ Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Uliyyah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, that Abu al-Abidin, a man from Banu Tamim who was blind, asked Ibn Mas'ud about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is withholding the axe and the bucket, or he said: withholding the axe and the cooking pot.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Hakam, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, that Abu al-Abidin asked Ibn Mas'ud about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is what people lend to one another: the axe, the cooking pot and the bucket.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Jawwab narrated to us, from Ammar ibn Ruzayq, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, from Abu al-Abidin, from Abdullah, who said: We, the companions of Muhammad, used to say that al-Ma'un is: the cooking pot, the axe and the bucket. Abu Bakr said: Abu al-Jawwab said, and Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah differed with him in what follows:

⁕ al-Hasan al-Ashyab narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from Harithah, from Abu al-Abidin. Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah, from Abu al-Abidin and Sa'id ibn Iyad, from Abdullah, who said: We, the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, used to say that al-Ma'un is: the bucket, the axe and the cooking pot, which one cannot do without.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Iyad — Abu Musa said: Ghundar said it thus — from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: Among al-Ma'un are: the axe, the bucket and the cooking pot.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Iyad, who narrates from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ the like of it.

⁕ He said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Iyad narrate from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.

⁕ Khallad narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, saying: Isra'il informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq informed us, from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, from Abu al-Abidin, who said: Abdullah said: al-Ma'un: the cooking pot, the axe and the bucket.

⁕ Khallad narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, saying: al-Mas'udi informed us, saying: Salamah ibn Kuhayl informed us, from Abu al-Abidin, who had a disability, and Abdullah used to recognise that about him, so he said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, what is al-Ma'un? He said: What people pass to one another among themselves, of the axe, the cooking pot, the bucket and the like of that.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim, from Abu al-Abidin, that he asked Ibn Mas'ud about al-Ma'un, and he said: What people pass to one another among themselves.

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from al-Hasan and Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Abidin, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The axe, the bucket, the cooking pot and the like of it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Abidin, that he asked Ibn Mas'ud about the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, and he related something similar.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The axe, the cooking pot and the bucket.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah, who said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: withholding the axe, the cooking pot and the bucket.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah, that he was asked about al-Ma'un, and he said: What people lend to one another: the axe, the bucket and the like.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The bucket, the axe and the cooking pot.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Iyad, from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: al-Ma'un: the axe, the cooking pot and the bucket.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah was asked about al-Ma'un, and he said: What people lend to one another: the axe, the cooking pot, the bucket and the like.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that he said: It is the lending of people: the axe, the cooking pot, the bucket and the like, meaning al-Ma'un.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, the like of it.

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it, who said: The axe and the bucket.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit al-Asadi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: the lending (al-ariyah).

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: It is the lending.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾, who said: The household goods (matá' al-bayt).

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, I think from Ibn Abbas — Abu Kurayb was in doubt — concerning ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, who said: The goods (al-mata').

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Uliyyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih informed us, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: It is the household goods.

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: They withhold from them the lending, and that is al-Ma'un.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, who said: People differed about that: some said they withhold the zakah, some said they withhold obedience, and some said they withhold the lending.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Uliyyah narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, who said: Its people have not yet come.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: what people pass to one another among themselves.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uliyyah informed us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: withholding the zakah, the axe, the bucket and the cooking pot.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim al-Nabil narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: al-Ma'un: the lending.

⁕ Abu Husayn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Malik, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, who said: The bucket, the cooking pot and the axe.

⁕ Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, who said: We were with our Prophet ﷺ, and we used to say: al-Ma'un: withholding the bucket and the like of that.

Others said: al-Ma'un is al-ma'ruf (kindness/beneficence).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b say: al-Ma'un: al-ma'ruf.

Others said: al-Ma'un is wealth (al-mal).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ahmad ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Al-ma'un, in the language of Quraysh, is wealth.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Zuhri, who said: Al-ma'un, in the language of Quraysh, is wealth.

The most correct of these opinions in our view is what we have described before: since al-Ma'un is what we have mentioned, and Allah informed about these people that they withhold it from people, in a general report without specifying any part of it, it should be said that Allah described them as withholding from people what they lend to one another, and withholding from the needy and the poor what Allah obligated for them in their wealth of rights; for all of that is among the benefits from which people benefit one another.

End of the tafsir of Surah Ara'ayta.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is His Mention and Sanctified are His Names: ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? That is the one who repulses the orphan, and does not urge the feeding of the needy. So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who make show [of their deeds], and withhold assistance.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, means by His words: ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾: Have you seen, O Muhammad, the one who denies Allah's reward and punishment, and so does not obey Him in His commands and prohibitions.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾ He said: The one who denies the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿denies the Recompense﴾, he said: the reckoning.

It is mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it is: "Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense" with the ب (ba') being a complementary particle (silah), its presence and absence in speech being the same.

* *

His words: ﴿That is the one who repulses the orphan﴾

He says: This one who denies the Recompense is the one who repulses the orphan from his right and wrongs him. It is said of this: "I repulsed so-and-so from his right," and I repulse him with a repulsion (da'a).

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿That is the one who repulses the orphan﴾, he said: He repels the orphan's right.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿repulses the orphan﴾, he said: he repulses the orphan and does not feed him.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿That is the one who repulses the orphan﴾: that is, he oppresses him and wrongs him.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿repulses the orphan﴾, he said: he oppresses him and wrongs him.

⁕ It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿repulses the orphan﴾, he said: he oppresses him.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding His words: ﴿repulses the orphan﴾, he said: he pushes him away.

* *

His words: ﴿and does not urge the feeding of the needy﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: and he does not urge others to feed the one in need from food.

* *

His words: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: So the valley that flows with the pus of the people of Hell is for the hypocrites who pray, not desiring Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with their prayer, and who are heedless of their prayer when they perform it.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿heedless of their prayer﴾. Some of them said: What is meant by this is that they delay it from its time, so they do not pray it except after its time has passed.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Sakan ibn Nafi' al-Bahili narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khalaf ibn Hawshab, from Talhah ibn Musarrif, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, who said: I said to my father: Have you seen the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾? Is it abandoning it? He said: No, but delaying it from its time.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, he said: Asim ibn Bahdalah narrated to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, who said: I said to Sa'd: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾ — is it what one of us speaks to himself about during his prayer? He said: No, but heedlessness is that one delays it from its time.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Asim, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: Heedlessness is leaving it beyond its time.

⁕ Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, he said: Imran ibn Tammam al-Bananai narrated to us, he said: Abu Jamrah al-Dab'i Nasr ibn Imran narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: Those who delay it from its time.

⁕ Ibn Humayd also narrated to us, he said: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abzá: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: Those who delay the prescribed prayer until it leaves its time, or beyond its time.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: Abandoning it at its time.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, regarding His words: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: Wasting its appointed time.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha: ﴿heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: Abandoning the prescribed prayer at its time.

⁕ Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, he said: Ibn Zahr informed me, from al-A'mash, from Muslim ibn Subayh: ﴿heedless of their prayer﴾, those who waste it beyond its time.

Others said: Rather, what is meant is that they abandon it and do not pray it.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾, they are the hypocrites who used to show off to people with their prayer when present, and abandon it when absent, and they withhold from them the lending of goods out of hatred for them, and this is al-Ma'un.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: They are the hypocrites who abandon the prayer in secret and pray openly.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: Abandoning it.

Others said: Rather, what is meant is that they treat it with negligence, are unmindful of it, and are distracted from it.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: Careless.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾: unmindful.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: Heedless of it, not caring whether he prayed or did not pray.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾: they pray, but prayer is not their concern.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, he said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: They treat it with negligence.

The most correct of the sayings in my view regarding the meaning of His words ﴿sahun (heedless)﴾ is: they are distracted, neglectful of it, and in their distraction from it and their preoccupation with other things, they waste it at times and waste its time at other times. If that is the case, the saying of the one who said that what is meant is the wasting of its time is valid, and the saying of the one who said that what is meant is abandoning it is also valid, because of what I mentioned, that heedlessness of it includes the meanings I have mentioned.

Two reports have been transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that support the soundness of what we have said:

The first of them:

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to me, he said: Amr ibn Tariq narrated to us, he said: Ikrimah ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr narrated to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about (﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾), and he said: They are those who delay the prayer beyond its time.

The other of them:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to me, he said: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Shaybān al-Nahwi, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: A man narrated to me, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾, Allahu Akbar! This is better for you than if each one of you were given the like of all the world; it is the one who, if he prays, does not hope for good from his prayer, and if he abandons it, does not fear his Lord."

⁕ Abu Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, he said: Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, he said: I heard Umar ibn Sulayman narrate from Ata' ibn Dinar that he said: Praise be to Allah who said: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾. And both meanings that you mentioned in the two reports we narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are possible regarding the meaning of heedlessness of the prayer.

* *

His words: ﴿Those who make show [of their deeds]﴾

He says: those who show off to people with their prayer when they pray, because they do not pray out of desire for reward or fear of punishment, but they pray so that the believers may see them and think them to be of them, and thus refrain from shedding their blood and taking their offspring captive. They are the hypocrites of the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who concealed disbelief and displayed Islam. So the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abu Amir and Mu'ammal narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer﴾, he said: They are the hypocrites.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), regarding His words: ﴿they make show and withhold al-Ma'un﴾, he said: They make show with their prayer.

⁕ It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿those who are heedless of their prayer, those who make show﴾, meaning the hypocrites.

⁕ Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, he said: They are the hypocrites, who used to show off to people with their prayer when present, and abandon it when absent.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd narrated to me: "and they pray, while prayer is not their concern, [doing so] for show."

* *

His words: ﴿and withhold al-Ma'un﴾

He says: and they withhold from people the benefits of what they possess. The root of al-Ma'un is the benefit of anything. Water that descends from the clouds is called ma'un, and from it is the saying of al-A'sha of Banu Tha'labah:

"More generous than him with his water, when their sky does not drizzle"

And another, describing a cloud:

"Its thin rain pours out the water, pouring"

And Ubayd al-Ra'i said:

"A people upon Islam who have not withheld their ma'un, and have not neglected the tahlil"

What is meant by al-Ma'un is obedience and zakah.

The people of interpretation differed regarding what is meant by al-Ma'un in this place. Some of them said: What is meant by it is the obligatory zakah.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, from Mujahid, he said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said regarding His words: ﴿and withhold al-Ma'un﴾: it is zakah.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, he said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: zakah.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us; and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: zakah.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Sufyan informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿and withhold al-Ma'un﴾, he said: They withhold the zakah of their wealth.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ammarah and Ahmad ibn Hisham narrated to me, both said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Israil informed us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿and withhold al-Ma'un﴾, he said: zakah.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾, he said: zakah.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ali, the like of it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: the obligatory charity.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and withhold al-Ma'un﴾, that Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: It is zakah.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, who said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: zakah.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Mughirah, who said: A man asked Ibn Umar about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is the wealth whose right is not paid. I said: Indeed Ibn Umm Abd says: It is the goods that people lend to one another. He said: It is what I tell you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 107, verse 1–7 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Salamah, who said: I heard Abu al-Mughirah say: I asked Ibn Umar about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is withholding the right (haqq).

⁕ Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, from Isma'il, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Ibn Umar was asked about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is the one who is asked for the right of his wealth and withholds it. He (the questioner) said: Ibn Mas'ud says: It is the cooking pot, the bucket and the axe. He said: That is what I say to you.

⁕ Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, that Ibn Umar was asked about the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾. He said: It is the one who is asked for the wealth of Allah and withholds it. The one who asked him said: Ibn Mas'ud says: It is the axe and the cooking pot. Ibn Umar said: That is what I say to you.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: A man asked Ibn Umar about al-Ma'un, and he related the like of it.

⁕ Sulayman ibn Muhammad ibn Ma'di Karib al-Ru'ayni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu al-Mughirah, a man from Banu Asad, say: I asked Abdullah ibn Umar about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is withholding the right. I said: Ibn Mas'ud said: It is withholding the axe and the bucket. He said: It is withholding the right.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Mughirah, from Ibn Umar, who said: It is the zakah.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ali, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Zayd ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from Hassan ibn Mukhariq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: the zakah.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah and al-Hasan: al-Ma'un: the obligatory zakah.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Umar, from Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: It is the zakah.

⁕ I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾: He said: The zakah.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾: They are the hypocrites who withhold the zakah of their wealth.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: the obligatory zakah.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Uqbah narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾: They withheld the charities of their wealth, so Allah reproached them for it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan: ﴿Those who make show [of their deeds] and withhold al-Ma'un﴾. He said: It is the hypocrite who withholds the zakah of his wealth. If he prays, he makes a show, and if he misses it, he does not regret it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Salamah, from al-Dahhak, who said: It is the zakah.

Others said: It is what people lend to one another among themselves, such as the bucket, the cooking pot and the like.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Hakam ibn Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from Abu al-Abidin, that he said to Abdullah: Inform me about al-Ma'un. He said: It is what people lend to one another among themselves.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Yahya ibn al-Jazzar narrate from Abu al-Abidin, a man from Banu Tamim who was blind, and who used to ask Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and Ibn Mas'ud would recognise that about him. He asked Abdullah about al-Ma'un, and Abdullah said: Among al-Ma'un is withholding the axe, the cooking pot and the bucket: two qualities out of these three. Shu'bah said: As for the axe, there is no doubt about it.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from Abu al-Abidin, from Abdullah, the like of it.

⁕ Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Uliyyah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, that Abu al-Abidin, a man from Banu Tamim who was blind, asked Ibn Mas'ud about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is withholding the axe and the bucket, or he said: withholding the axe and the cooking pot.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Hakam, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, that Abu al-Abidin asked Ibn Mas'ud about al-Ma'un, and he said: It is what people lend to one another: the axe, the cooking pot and the bucket.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Jawwab narrated to us, from Ammar ibn Ruzayq, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, from Abu al-Abidin, from Abdullah, who said: We, the companions of Muhammad, used to say that al-Ma'un is: the cooking pot, the axe and the bucket. Abu Bakr said: Abu al-Jawwab said, and Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah differed with him in what follows:

⁕ al-Hasan al-Ashyab narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from Harithah, from Abu al-Abidin. Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah, from Abu al-Abidin and Sa'id ibn Iyad, from Abdullah, who said: We, the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, used to say that al-Ma'un is: the bucket, the axe and the cooking pot, which one cannot do without.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Iyad — Abu Musa said: Ghundar said it thus — from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: Among al-Ma'un are: the axe, the bucket and the cooking pot.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Iyad, who narrates from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ the like of it.

⁕ He said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Iyad narrate from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.

⁕ Khallad narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, saying: Isra'il informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq informed us, from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, from Abu al-Abidin, who said: Abdullah said: al-Ma'un: the cooking pot, the axe and the bucket.

⁕ Khallad narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, saying: al-Mas'udi informed us, saying: Salamah ibn Kuhayl informed us, from Abu al-Abidin, who had a disability, and Abdullah used to recognise that about him, so he said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, what is al-Ma'un? He said: What people pass to one another among themselves, of the axe, the cooking pot, the bucket and the like of that.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim, from Abu al-Abidin, that he asked Ibn Mas'ud about al-Ma'un, and he said: What people pass to one another among themselves.

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from al-Hasan and Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Abidin, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The axe, the bucket, the cooking pot and the like of it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Abidin, that he asked Ibn Mas'ud about the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, and he related something similar.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The axe, the cooking pot and the bucket.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah, who said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: withholding the axe, the cooking pot and the bucket.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah, that he was asked about al-Ma'un, and he said: What people lend to one another: the axe, the bucket and the like.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The bucket, the axe and the cooking pot.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Iyad, from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: al-Ma'un: the axe, the cooking pot and the bucket.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah was asked about al-Ma'un, and he said: What people lend to one another: the axe, the cooking pot, the bucket and the like.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that he said: It is the lending of people: the axe, the cooking pot, the bucket and the like, meaning al-Ma'un.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, the like of it.

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it, who said: The axe and the bucket.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit al-Asadi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: the lending (al-ariyah).

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: It is the lending.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾, who said: The household goods (matá' al-bayt).

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, I think from Ibn Abbas — Abu Kurayb was in doubt — concerning ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, who said: The goods (al-mata').

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Uliyyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih informed us, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: It is the household goods.

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: They withhold from them the lending, and that is al-Ma'un.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, who said: People differed about that: some said they withhold the zakah, some said they withhold obedience, and some said they withhold the lending.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Uliyyah narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, who said: Its people have not yet come.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: what people pass to one another among themselves.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uliyyah informed us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: ﴿al-Ma'un﴾: withholding the zakah, the axe, the bucket and the cooking pot.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim al-Nabil narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: al-Ma'un: the lending.

⁕ Abu Husayn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Malik, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And they withhold al-Ma'un﴾, who said: The bucket, the cooking pot and the axe.

⁕ Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, who said: We were with our Prophet ﷺ, and we used to say: al-Ma'un: withholding the bucket and the like of that.

Others said: al-Ma'un is al-ma'ruf (kindness/beneficence).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b say: al-Ma'un: al-ma'ruf.

Others said: al-Ma'un is wealth (al-mal).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ahmad ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Al-ma'un, in the language of Quraysh, is wealth.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Zuhri, who said: Al-ma'un, in the language of Quraysh, is wealth.

The most correct of these opinions in our view is what we have described before: since al-Ma'un is what we have mentioned, and Allah informed about these people that they withhold it from people, in a general report without specifying any part of it, it should be said that Allah described them as withholding from people what they lend to one another, and withholding from the needy and the poor what Allah obligated for them in their wealth of rights; for all of that is among the benefits from which people benefit one another.

End of the tafsir of Surah Ara'ayta.
